title: Paid family and medical leave
summary: AB 388 would have required private employers with 50+ Nevada employees to fund up to 12 weeks of qualifying leave. The sponsor has floated a broader state-run model for 2027.
watch_for: Model employer contributions and backfill costs; check the funding split and small-employer rules once text is published.

title: Right to work and employer meetings
summary: Governor-elect Ford reaffirmed his pledge to repeal right to work, which could allow union-security terms in covered bargaining. AB 434 would have allowed damages for penalizing employees who skip certain political or religious meetings, including some labor organization discussions.
watch_for: Watch whether a repeal bill and an AB 434 successor are filed, and how they treat unionized jobsites.

title: Pricing and antitrust enforcement
summary: SB 31 would limit certain surge and personalized pricing at large grocery stores and raise the state antitrust civil penalty ceiling to $50,000 per violation. AB 44 targeted deceptive pricing on essentials, including housing.
watch_for: Track the penalty change and any housing-related pricing provisions.

title: Workplace bullying and civil liability
summary: Would require procedures to prevent, investigate and resolve workplace bullying complaints, protect against retaliation and allow civil suits.
watch_for: Watch how it defines unlawful conduct and treats supervisors and multiple employers on one jobsite.

title: Residential evictions and investor purchases
summary: AB 283 would have required landlords to file first in covered summary evictions. Ford also proposes a one-month security deposit cap, tighter rental fees and limits on some corporate home purchases.
watch_for: For multifamily owners and developers, watch which properties and transactions are covered.

title: Data center expansion and incentives
reference: Interim Revenue Committee draft · Ford proposals
summary: The interim Revenue Committee voted to draft a moratorium on new or expanded data centers and repeal their tax abatements. Ford proposed pausing new abatements pending an audit and charging operators for added grid costs.
watch_for: Track how each approach treats projects already permitted, financed or under contract.

title: Prevailing wage and tax incentive conditions
reference: 2025 AB 213 and AB 226 (vetoed) · Ford supports prevailing wage
summary: AB 213 would have extended prevailing wage to custom fabrication for covered public projects and tied some bid preferences to in-state fabrication. AB 226 would have attached community-benefit agreements and other conditions to certain abatements.
watch_for: Estimating should track off-site fabrication and subcontractor pricing exposure.

title: Air quality at large hybrid facilities
summary: Covered facilities of 10,000+ square feet with more than 15 workers; would have required air monitoring and logging at least every four hours plus engine-off loading rules.
watch_for: Check whether any Burke-built or operated facilities would qualify based on outdoor exposure during shifts.

title: Fertility coverage and prescription pricing
summary: SB 217 would have required fertility treatment and preservation coverage for some group plans over 50 members. AB 259 would have applied Medicare-negotiated limits to certain drug purchases.
watch_for: Benefits staff should check plan applicability if successors are filed.

title: Tax on digital products and subscriptions
reference: Interim Revenue Committee draft · 2025 SB 392 precedent
summary: A tax on certain electronically delivered products and subscriptions could add collection duties for sellers and platforms. Revenue increases generally need two-thirds in each chamber.
watch_for: Watch the definition of taxable products and who collects.

title: Construction manager at risk procurement
summary: The State Public Works Division requested changes to construction manager at risk rules.
watch_for: Compare the bill and amendments with selection, preconstruction and subcontracting procedures on upcoming public bids.

title: Groundwater fees and development approvals
summary: Would let qualifying counties in designated basins charge up to $30 per acre-foot of permitted groundwater by a two-thirds county vote, and revise some monitoring, mitigation and water-right change procedures.
watch_for: Exposure depends on each project's basin and water supply.

title: Employer payroll and work records
summary: Would require employers to keep unemployment work records listing occupation, hours worked and reported tips alongside pay rates and total wages. It also revises funding for certain employment and job training programs and lets some pupils train through them.
watch_for: Payroll should confirm records capture these fields consistently; workforce development may want to track the training-program funding changes.

title: Enforcement of workplace discrimination claims
summary: Would have moved the Nevada Equal Rights Commission into the Attorney General's office and set an 18-month deadline for resolving investigated complaints, with exceptions.
watch_for: Could change case handling and the timing of employer responses.

title: Hospital staffing ratios
summary: Would have set nurse staffing ratios for hospitals over 70 beds in counties of 100,000+ residents and expanded staffing committees and reporting.
watch_for: Higher staffing costs could affect hospital owners' operating and capital budgets.

title: Human review of health insurance decisions
reference: 2025 SB 128 (vetoed) · Ford supports limits on insurer AI
summary: Would have barred covered insurers from relying solely on AI to deny or modify certain prior authorizations.
watch_for: Raise implementation with benefits providers if a successor bill moves.

title: Hotel and resort incident reporting
summary: Would require hotels, resort hotels and some public agencies to keep and report incidents quarterly, from emergency responses to guest evictions.
watch_for: Relevant to hospitality clients and resort projects.

title: Live entertainment ticket resale tax
reference: Interim Revenue Committee draft · 2025 SB 431 precedent
summary: The committee discussed extending the Live Entertainment Tax to regular ticket resales, taxing the resale markup.
watch_for: Venue and sports clients should watch the taxable amount, exemptions and collection duties.

title: Real estate entity taxation
summary: A legislated study of combining related property rental businesses for Commerce Tax and taxing transfers of controlling interests in entities that own Nevada real estate.
watch_for: A resulting bill could affect entity structuring and transaction costs on development deals.

title: Contractor notices
summary: The State Contractors' Board requested revisions to certain contractor notices; the public summary doesn't yet say which notices or projects.
watch_for: Check recipients, deadlines and consequences once text is out, especially notices tied to payment or claims.
